ORDER The present petition under Article 226 of Constitution of India has been filed seeking a mandamus directing the respondents to pay the amount of compensation in terms of the Award dated 13/11/2018 passed by respondent No.2/ Collector Jabalpur, which was initially passed taking into consideration the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency of Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act of 2013').
2.

No compensation was given pertaining to the said land to the petitioners.
Therefore, they preferred a Writ Petition before this Court being W.P. No.21481/2013.
During the pendency of the Writ Petition, respondent No.4 published a Gazette notification dated 06/05/2016, imposing sweeping restrictions on the use of land, de facto acquiring the land.

The said Writ Petition was disposed of vide order dated 30/08/2017 observing that the Authorities are required to proceed in terms of Sections 4 and 5 of the Works of Defence Act, 1903 (hereinafter Kewal Kumkar Jaggi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165852322/

Respondents No.3 and 4 failed to comply with the order dated 30/08/2017 and the petitioners were compelled to file a Contempt Petition No.1014/2018, which was disposed of vide order dated 06/04/2018 granting further 6 months' time to comply with the directions given by the Court vide order dated 30/08/2017 passed in W.P. No.21481/2013.
Respondents again failed to comply with the orders.
Therefore, petitioners again preferred a Contempt Petition No.2959/2018 before this Court.
During the pendency of the Content Petition, Collector Jabalpur by order dated 13/11/2018 passed an Award determining the compensation to the tune of Rs.10,55,51,600/-.
However, due to the objection taken by the respondents No.3 and 4

, Collector has NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:70517 3 WP-21788-2021 recalled the Award and passed a fresh Award dated 25/01/2019 reducing the compensation to Rs.6,06,92,170/-.
The same was again objected by respondents No.3 and 4.
Therefore, the matter was reconsidered by the Collector and third Award dated 03/08/2019 was passed determining the compensation to the tune of Rs.5,51,74,700/-.
This was again objected by respondents No.3 and 4 which resulted into passing of another Award by the Collector determining the compensation to the tune of Rs.1,96,97,200/-.

After passing of the first Award on 13/11/2018, respondents No.3 and 4 are continuously raising objections that the Award is to be passed taking note of the WODA Act, 1903 and not in terms of the Act of 2013.
Respondents No.3 and 4 also filed an application seeking extension of 6 weeks' time for making the payments.

Another application was filed seeking exemption from personal appearance on 30/09/2019, which makes it abundantly clear that the compensation is to be determined under the provisions of the WODA Act, 1903.

3 . It is the case of the petitioners that the Defence Authorities are dictating the entire process for determination of the Award and the Collector is passing repeated Awards on the instructions of the Defence Authorities without even providing any opportunity of hearing to the petitioners.
When the first award was passed on 13/11/2018, there was no occasion to the Collector to recall the said Award and pass a fresh Award.
It is their case that the Collector becomes functus officio after passing of Award on 13/11/2018.
There cannot be any re-determination of the Award by the Collector.
Considering the aforesaid, Contempt Petition No.2959/2018 was disposed of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:70517 4 WP-21788-2021 vide order dated 21/11/2019.

4 . Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners has heavily relied upon Section 2 of the Act of 2013 and has argued that the provisions of the Act of 2013 relating to land acquisition, compensation,
rehabilitation and resettlement shall apply when the appropriate Government acquires land for its own use, hold and control including for public sector undertaking and for public purposes.

It is argued that from Section 2, it is abundantly clear that Act of 2013 will have application over the provisions of the WODA Act 1903, wherein it specifically contemplates the word "hold and control".
He has also placed before this Court the statement and object and provisions of WODA Act, 1903 and has argued that the same does not leave any room for speculation.

It is argued that from the Kewal Kumkar Jaggi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165852322/
2 bare reading of the statement and object of the WODA Act 1903 as well as Section 2(1) of the Act of 2013, it is abundantly clear that the Act of 2013 would be applicable for determining compensation qua the WODA Act 1903.

He has drawn attention of this Court to Section 105 of the Act of 2013,
which provides that the same shall not apply in certain cases or to apply in certain modifications subject to sub- section (3) and shall not apply to the enactment relating to the land acquisition specified under the 4th Schedule wherein WODA Act 1903 is not included.

5. It is argued that initially when the Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Bill, 2011 was prepared and presented before the Lok Sabha, the application of Act of 2013 was sought to be excluded over the provisions of WODA Act 1903.

sentences.text: However, on the request of the Ministry of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:70517 5 WP-21788-2021 Defence, the Cantonment Act and WODA Act 1903 were deleted from the list of 4th Schedule of 2013.

Thus, the objections raised by the Authorities that the provisions of WODA Act 1903 are applicable has resulted in passing of multiple Awards by the Collector and has caused grave injustice to the petitioners.

It is also pointed out that there was another Contempt Petition No.708 of 2020 was filed, which was finally disposed of vide order dated 24/06/2021 directing the Collector to release the amount to the petitioners.
During the pendency of Contempt Petition No.708 of 2020, respondents No.3 and 4 filed a Reference under Section 18 of the WODA Act 1903 against the Award dated 27/09/2019.
The same was duly forwarded to the District Judge, Jabalpur and registered as MJC No.283 of 2021 in the name of Union of India and Another Vs. Kewal Kumar Jaggi and others.

sentences.text: Respondents No.3 and 4 approached the Hon'ble Supreme Court by filing SLP No.8579/2021 against the order dated 24/06/2021 passed in Contempt Petition No.708 of 2020, which was disposed of setting aside the order passed in Contempt Petition No.708 of 2020 dated 24/06/2021 and certain directions were issued by the Hon'ble Supreme Court vide order dated 08/07/2021.

After passing of the order by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, a preliminary objection raised by the petitioners before Reference Court was rejected and the disbursal of the Award amount was stayed vide order dated 26/07/2021, which was subject matter of challenge in M.P. No.2493 of 2021 which is pending consideration before this Court.

It is the case of the petitioners that seminal issue as to the applicability of the Act of 2013 in the matter of determination of compensation under the WODA Act 1903 needs NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:70517 6 WP-21788-2021 to be determined independently on original side.
Therefore, this petition is filed.

6 . It is the specific case of the petitioners that the Collector after passing of the first Award dated 13/11/2018 has become functus officio and therefore, could not have entertained any objections filed by the respondents.
Therefore, the subsequent Awards passed by the Collector are void ab initio and non est in the eyes of law.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has drawn attention of this Court to the fact that the restrictions have been imposed upon the petitioners not even to enter their land which virtually amounts to forceful acquisition of the land by the respondents without payment of any compensation to the petitioners.

Once the Authorities have already determined the compensation,
the same should have been paid to the petitioner as there is specific provision under Section 34 of the WODA Act, 1903 which mandates the payment/ release of amount of Award within 15 days from the date of deposition and the Collector has no authority to withhold, deny the payment of Award to the beneficiaries.

In pursuance to the direction given by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, petitioners have preferred objections before the Reference Court pointing out that the Reference filed by the Kewal Kumkar Jaggi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165852322/
3 Defence Authorities under Section 18 of the WODA Act, 1903 is not maintainable as the Defence Authorities does not fall under the category of person interested.

sentences.text: Secondly, section 25(3) of the WODA Act 1903 provides that the amount awarded by the Collector shall not be reduced, it can only be exceeded.
Therefore, the Reference made by respondents No.3 and 4 is not maintainable.

However, such objection was rejected by the Reference Court NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:70517 7 WP-21788-2021 vide order dated 26/07/2021.
Therefore, this petition has been filed.
7 . On notice being issued, a reply has been filed by the respondents taking a preliminary objection with respect to the maintainability of the petition.

It is pointed out that the earlier Writ Petition filed before this Court was disposed of in the year 2017 with certain directions regarding computation/
calculation of compensation to be made to the petitioners and liberty was extended to the petitioners to challenge the notification under Section 3 of the WODA Act, 1903.

After the series of litigation, the matter traveled up to the Hon'ble Supreme Court in SLP No.8579/2021, wherein it was observed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that the High Court has exceeded its powers while deciding the Contempt Petition.
After passing of the third Award by the Collector, respondents preferred an application under Section 18 of the WODA Act, 1903 seeking Reference to be made to the District Court.
Petitioners were aware of passing of order by the Collector whereby he had duly referred the matter to the District Judge for determination of the Award.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court while disposing of the SLP has rightly decided the question of maintainability of the Reference proceedings and held that Reference Petition to be maintained maintainable in accordance with law.
It was further observed that the petitioners till date have not approached the respondents Authorities seeking permission to carry out any activity on the land.

It is contended that once the Hon'ble Supreme Court has decided the matter and had granted liberty to the petitioners to raise all objections as well as to file a Reference before the District Judge for enhancement of the compensation, the question of maintainability of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:70517 8 WP-21788-2021 Reference before the District Judge does not arise anymore and will be hit by the principles of constructive res judicata and estoppel.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in SLP has taken note of the entire litigation between the parties with respect to the land in question and after considering the series of litigation between the parties, the Hon'ble Supreme Court recognized the fact that the compensation has to be calculated under the WODA Act,
1903 and not under the Act of 2013.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court has noted the finding "finding merits in the said objection the Collector undertook the fresh exercise".

Thus, after the order filed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court and in terms of the direction given by the Hon'ble Supreme Court therein, the petitioners were required to raise all the objections before the Reference Court and the Reference Court was directed to decide all the objections prior to passing final order in Reference on merits.
Petitioners were also granted liberty to file a Reference before the District Judge for enhancement of compensation.
It is pointed out that the Reference before the District Judge is still pending consideration.
The objections raised by the petitioners were rejected by the District Judge vide order dated 26/07/2021.
Therefore, the present petition now seeking determination of applicability of the Act of 2013 over and above the WODA Act, 2003 is not maintainable.

8. He has also drawn attention of this Court to the observations made by this Court while disposing of W.P. No.21481/2013 vide order dated 30/08/2017 which is not put to challenge by the petitioners Kewal Kumkar Jaggi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165852322/
4 at any point of time and which was disposed of with the following directions:-
"(i) That the respondents shall take appropriate steps to determine the damages and payment of damages to the petitioners on account of imposition of restrictions in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:70517 9 WP-21788-2021 regard to use of lands after publication of notification under Section 3 of the Act of 1903 within a period of six months from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
( ii )

If the respondents fail to pay damages and will not determine the same within the stipulated period, the petitioners are at liberty to take appropriate action and they are at liberty to file appropriate proceedings in accordance with law.
The petitioners can also challenge the notification issued under Section 3 of the Act of 1903 quoted above in the order."
9. From the perusal of the aforesaid, it is clear that the determination of damages and payment of damages is to be ascertained in terms of WODA Act, 1903.
Liberty was extended to the petitioners to challenge the notification issued under the WODA Act, 1903 under Section 3 of WODA Act, 1903.

The said order has attained finality as the same was not put to challenge by the petitioners.
10.

Petitioners have filed a rejoinder to the aforesaid reiterating the submissions, to which an additional affidavit in the form of counter affidavit is filed placing on record the Central Government notification dated 06/05/2016 imposing restrictions specified in clause (b) of Section 7 of the WODA Act, 1903 upon the use and enjoyment of the land described in Schedule being land lying in the vicinity of Military Station in Sukhlalpur in District Jabalpur.
The said notification is not put to challenge at any point of time.
He has heavily relied upon the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in SLP (Civil) No.8579 of 2021.

It is also brought to the notice of this Court that the 10th Additional District Judge, Jabalpur vide its order dated 26/07/2021 has held that the Reference application was maintainable and stayed the disbursement of Award till the finalization of Reference proceeding which was put to challenge before this Court in M.P. NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:70517 10 WP-21788-2021 No.2493/2021 and vide order dated 17/11/2021,
the petition was allowed holding that the Reference petition is not maintainable.

Against which,
respondents preferred SLP (Civil) No.19456 of 2021, wherein notices were issued and the operation of the order passed in M.P. No.2493/2021 was stayed vide order dated 03/12/2021.
The same is pending consideration.

Therefore, until and unless the lis is finally decided by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, no observations can be made with respect to applicability of the Act of 2013 as the petitioner is free to raise all the grounds either before the Reference Court or before the Hon'ble Supreme Court.

The record shows that SLP was lastly listed on 19/04/2024 and is pending consideration wherein permission was granted to the respondents to withdraw an amount of Rs.50,00,000/-
(Rupees Fifty Lakhs Only) from the Collector (Land Acquisition), Jabalpur out of the amount of Rs.1,96,97,200/- (Rupees One Crore Ninety Six Lakhs Ninety Seven Thousand and Two Hundred only) deposited by the Ministry of Defence.

sentences.text: From the perusal of the record, it is seen that there are series of litigation between the parties.
The land of the petitioners has been put to restrictions exercising relevant provisions under the WODA Act, 1903.

For the sake of convenience, a chronology of dates and events as well as series of litigation undertaken by the parties is reproduced as under:-
The Works of Defence Act, 1903 was enacted.

It provides inter- alia power to the Central Govt to issue notification restricting 1903 the use of land in the vicinity of Defence installations up to prescribed distance and compensation to land owner for such restricted use of land.

That in the year 2013, the Respondents preferred Writ Petition NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:70517 11 WP-21788-2021 In 2013 No.21481 of 2013 not to disturb or restrain the petitioners and to restrain authorities from interfering in using of the Land by the Petitioners.

Writ Petition No.

That immediately after the expiry of 6 months, the Respondents 22.10.2018 preferred 2nd Contempt Petition before the Hon'ble High Court, being Conc No. 2959 of 2018.

From the perusal of the aforesaid directions passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, it is apparently clear that the Hon'ble Supreme Court has made observations that the Collector has incorrectly invoked the provisions of the Act of 2013 when the entire proceedings of imposition of restrictions have taken place in terms of the WODA Act, 1903.

10th Additional District Judge Jabalpur i.e. Reference Court on 26/07/2021 rejected the objections taken by the petitioners herein regarding maintainability of Reference and held that the Reference is maintainable and also stayed the disbursement of Award amount till the finalization of Reference proceedings which was subject matter of challenge before this Court in M.P. The withdrawal shall not require any security and shall not prejudice the case of any of the parties."
15.

In view of the directions given by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in first SLP i.e. SLP (C)
No.8579/2021 as well as the fact that second SLP i.e. SLP(C) No.19456/2021 which is pending consideration wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court is yet to determine the question of maintainability of Reference, this Court does not deem it appropriate to determine the question raised in this petition regarding applicability of Act of 2013 while determining the damages or the restrictions which are imposed on the petitioners regarding use of their land as the said aspect can be clarified by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the pending SLP.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court has already permitted the withdrawal of amount of Rs.50,00,000/- to the petitioners.

Therefore,
petitioners may raise all the grounds raised in this petition before the Hon'ble Supreme Court in pending SLP regarding applicability of the Act of 2013 for the purpose of determination of compensation.

opennyai_summary.PREAMBLE:
Kewal Kumkar Jaggi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7
October, 2025
Author: Vishal Mishra
Bench: Vishal Mishra  NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:70517  1   IN THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT JABALPUR  BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE VISHAL MISHRA  ON THE 7 th OF OCTOBER, 2025  WRIT PETITION No. 21788 of 2021  KEWAL KUMKAR JAGGI AND OTHERS  Versus  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 Shri Manoj Kumar Sharma - Senior Advocate with Shri Q  Fakhruddin and Ms. Lavanya Verma - Advocates for the petition
opennyai_summary.facts:
ORDER The present petition under Article 226 of Constitution of India has been filed seeking a mandamus directing the respondents to pay the amount of compensation in terms of the Award dated 13/11/2018 passed by respondent No.2/ Collector Jabalpur, which was initially passed taking into consideration the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency of Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act of 2013').
2.
During the pendency of the Writ Petition, respondent No.4 published a Gazette notification dated 06/05/2016, imposing sweeping restrictions on the use of land, de facto acquiring the land.
The said Writ Petition was disposed of vide order dated 30/08/2017 observing that the Authorities are required to proceed in terms of Sections 4 and 5 of the Works of Defence Act, 1903 (hereinafter Kewal Kumkar Jaggi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165852322/
1 referred to as 'WODA Act, 1903 ') and further to take appropriate steps to determine the damages on account of imposition of restrictions with respect to use of land within a period of 6 months and liberty was extended
that in case the directions are not complied with, then the petitioners can challenge the notification issued under Section 3 of the WODA Act, 1903.
When the first award was passed on 13/11/2018, there was no occasion to the Collector to recall the said Award and pass a fresh Award.
During the pendency of Contempt Petition No.708 of 2020, respondents No.3 and 4 filed a Reference under Section 18 of the WODA Act 1903 against the Award dated 27/09/2019.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
6 . It is the specific case of the petitioners that the Collector after passing of the first Award dated 13/11/2018 has become functus officio and therefore, could not have entertained any objections filed by the respondents.
Therefore, the subsequent Awards passed by the Collector are void ab initio and non est in the eyes of law.
Once the Authorities have already determined the compensation,
the same should have been paid to the petitioner as there is specific provision under Section 34 of the WODA Act, 1903 which mandates the payment/ release of amount of Award within 15 days from the date of deposition and the Collector has no authority to withhold, deny the payment of Award to the beneficiaries.
In pursuance to the direction given by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, petitioners have preferred objections before the Reference Court pointing out that the Reference filed by the Kewal Kumkar Jaggi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165852322/
3 Defence Authorities under Section 18 of the WODA Act, 1903 is not maintainable as the Defence Authorities does not fall under the category of person interested.
Secondly, section 25(3) of the WODA Act 1903 provides that the amount awarded by the Collector shall not be reduced, it can only be exceeded.
Therefore, the Reference made by respondents No.3 and 4 is not maintainable.
opennyai_summary.decision:
If the respondents fail to pay damages and will not determine the same within the stipulated period, the petitioners are at liberty to take appropriate action and they are at liberty to file appropriate proceedings in accordance with law.
9. From the perusal of the aforesaid, it is clear that the determination of damages and payment of damages is to be ascertained in terms of WODA Act, 1903.
The said order has attained finality as the same was not put to challenge by the petitioners.
10.
Against which,
respondents preferred SLP (Civil) No.19456 of 2021, wherein notices were issued and the operation of the order passed in M.P. No.2493/2021 was stayed vide order dated 03/12/2021.
That on 06.05.2016 the Central Govt. issued the Gazette Notification imposing restrictions,
Specified in clause (b) of section 7 of the Works of Defence Act 1903 upon the use and 06.05.2016 enjoyment of the land described in the schedule annexed being land lying in the vicinity of Military Station Sukhlalpur, in the District of Jabalpur in the State of Madhya Pradesh.
Writ Petition No.
21481 of 2013 was disposed of directing interalia, the authorities to determine the damages and payment 30.08.2016 of damages to the writ petitioners on account of imposition of restrictions under Section 3 of the Act of 1903 within a period of six months.
The Respondents filed first Contempt Petition No. 1014 of 2018 against the Petitioners herein for non-compliance of the order 28.03.2018 dated 30.08.2017 passed by the Hon'ble High Court in W.P. No. 21481 Of 2013 That the aforesaid Contempt Petition No. 1014 of 2018 the Hon'ble High Court was pleased to pass the following orders:-
"Under these circumstances, the competent authority is directed to comply with the order passed by this Court on 30.08.2017 in W.P. No. 21481/2013 within a further period of six months from 06.04.2018 the date of receipt of certified copy of this order and if the order is not complied with within the aforesaid period and the petitioners are again compelled to file another contempt petition, then the cost of the present contempt petition as well as the contempt petition which may be filed by the petitioners shall be recovered from the erring Officer."
That immediately after the expiry of 6 months, the Respondents 22.10.2018 preferred 2nd Contempt Petition before the Hon'ble High Court, being Conc No. 2959 of 2018.
That without going in to the fact that the present proceedings governed by the Work of Defence Act 1903 and not by the Land 13.11.2018 Acquisition Act. 1894, on 13.11.2018 erroneously the Collector (Land Acquisition) Jabalpur made an initial award of Rs. 10,55,51,600/- under the Land Acquisition Act. 1894.
That thereafter the Petitioners filed the Counter Affidavit dated 17.12.2008 17.12.2018 in Conc No. 2959 of 2018 before the Hon'ble High Court.
That while the Conc No. 2959 of 2018 was pending adjudication, without going in to the fact that the present proceedings governed by the Work of Defence Act. 1903 on 29.01.2019 25.01.2019 the Collector (Land Acquisition) Jabalpur, while correcting the earlier calculation, made an erroneous award of Rs. 6,06,92,170/- without applying the provisions of Section 23 NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:70517 12 WP-21788-2021 and 24 of the Works and Defence Act.
That thereafter the Collector filed a Compliance Report dated 31.01.2019 31.01.2019 in Conc No.
2959 of 2018 before the Hon'ble High Court.
That vide order dated 21.11.2019 the Hon'ble High Court 21.11.2019 dismissed the Conc No. 2959 of 2018 by the Respondents.
That thereafter without going in the facts and circumstances of the case that the matter is already sub-judice before the Reference Court, in view of the Application filed by the Petitioner under section 18 of the Works of Defence Act, 1903, 18.08.2020 and without considering the Status report filed by the Petitioner
That thereafter in pursuance of the order dated 15.10.2020 passed by the Hon'ble High Court in Conc No 708/2020 on 03.11.2020 03.11.2020, an amount of Rs 1,96,97,200/- was sanctioned by the President of India under the Provision of Works of Defence Act, 1903.
After the completion of pleadings the Conc. Case No.708 of 2020 was listed for hearing on 24.06.2021 before the Hon'ble High Court, wherein going beyond the Contempt Jurisdiction,
24.06.2021 and the compliance of order for which the contempt was filed, the Hon' ble High Court vide order dated 24.06.2021 directed for disbursal of amount of Rs.1,96,97,200/- deposited with the collector to the Respondents.
i.e. the reference court vide order dated 26.07.2021 held that the 26.07.2021 reference application was maintainable and stayed the disbursal of the award amount till the finalization of the reference proceedings.
The Hon'ble High Court vide impugned order dated 17.11.2021 17.11.2021 allowed the petition and held that the reference petition is not maintainable.
Special Leave Petition (Civil) Number 19456/2021 was heard on 03.12.2021 03.12.2021 and notice was issued and the operation of the impugned judgment of MP 2493/2021 was stayed.
Initially in SLP (C) No.8579/2021, which was preferred by the respondents herein, order dated 24/06/2021 passed in Conc. No.708/2020 was put to challenge,
which was allowed with the following observations:-
"14.
However, for doing complete justice and for ensuring that there is no further confusion, we are inclined to pass the following directions:
(a) The reference petition pending before the 29Additional District Judge, Jabalpur in Case No.MJC/6337/2020 CNR MP200L0195912020 filed by the appellants against the determination of compensation amount by the Collector, Jabalpur, be decided expeditiously and in accordance with law.
(b) The respondents would be also at liberty to file a reference before the District Judge for enhancement of the compensation.
(d) It will be open to the appellants to apply for stay against disbursement of the compensation amount lying deposited with the Collector, Jabalpur.
Such applications be decided on its own merits and in accordance with law.
Direction was issued to 29th Additional District Judge, Jabalpur to decide the Reference expeditiously in accordance with law.
Before proceeding the matter on merits, the Court may decide the objection taken by the respondents in the Reference regarding maintainability of the Reference.
Petitioners herein were also granted liberty to file Reference before the District Judge for enhancement of compensation.
10th Additional District Judge Jabalpur i.e. Reference Court on 26/07/2021 rejected the objections taken by the petitioners herein regarding maintainability of Reference and held that the Reference is maintainable and also stayed the disbursement of Award amount till the finalization of Reference proceedings which was subject matter of challenge before this Court in M.P. No.2493/2021 which was allowed on 17/11/2021 holding that Reference petition is not maintainable.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:70517 15 WP-21788-2021 The said order was put to challenge by the respondents before the Hon'ble Supreme Court in SLP (Civil) No.19456/2021,
wherein on 03/12/2021 notices were issued and impugned order dated 17/11/2021 passed in M.P.
No.2493/2021 was stayed.
The said SLP is still pending consideration before the Hon'ble Supreme Court and was lastly listed on 19/04/2024, wherein following order was passed:-
"In the meantime, the respondents are given liberty to withdraw an amount of Rs.50,00,000/- (Rupees Fifty Lakhs Only) from the Collector (Land Acquisition),
Jabalpur out of the amount of Rs.1,96,97,200/- (Rupees One Crore Ninety Six Lakhs Ninety Seven Thousand and Two Hundred only) deposited by the Ministry of Defence.
The withdrawal shall not require any security and shall not prejudice the case of any of the parties."
15.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court has already permitted the withdrawal of amount of Rs.50,00,000/- to the petitioners.
Therefore,
petitioners may raise all the grounds raised in this petition before the Hon'ble Supreme Court in pending SLP regarding applicability of the Act of 2013 for the purpose of determination of compensation.
Under these circumstances, no relief can be extended to the petitioners as the determination of compensation to the petitioners shall be subject to outcome of the orders passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in pending SLP.
17.
Accordingly, the petition fails and is hereby dismissed.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Liberty was extended to the petitioners to challenge the notification issued under the WODA Act, 1903 under Section 3 of WODA Act, 1903.
In view of the directions given by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in first SLP i.e. SLP (C)
No.8579/2021 as well as the fact that second SLP i.e. SLP(C) No.19456/2021 which is pending consideration wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court is yet to determine the question of maintainability of Reference, this Court does not deem it appropriate to determine the question raised in this petition regarding applicability of Act of 2013 while determining the damages or the restrictions which are imposed on the petitioners regarding use of their land as the said aspect can be clarified by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the pending SLP.
